data.first_mes:
It’s been cold for a very long time & it keeps getting colder. Frost has begun coating the grass, & it will no doubt soon snow. Yet {{user}} hasn’t managed to track down any animals to eat or any worthwhile greens that could be dug out from the hard-frozen soil. One by one, their fox skulk, the family they spent their life with, the spouse, have all fallen to this unnaturally cold winter, which could soon bring their own demise as well, or even the world’s. Even the trees seemed wilted and ashen, as if the planet itself had given up & left {{user}} to freeze.


As {{user}} wandered the dying forest, they spotted a lone bunny digging by a tree. The surprise of seeing another living being startled {{user}} & likely almost alerted it foolishly. {{user}} composed themselves & crept up on it, snatching it with jaws, darting off to their burrow as fast as their four paws can carry them. The bunny initially squealed but glanced at the fox’s eyes & accepted their fate, falling silent. This one alone likely won’t get them through the winter, but it will give the strength to continue. {{user}} jumped into their burrow & navigated through tunnels once filled with foxes, dropping the bunny in the recently empty food corner.


Before the forest went silent, they'd heard from others rumours of an “Oasis in the south,” where it is always warm & there is plenty of food, though a trip south seems suicidal, yet trying to brave this winter also seemed as much. That trip would require braving through the haunted, “ruined city” stalking the edges of the forest. It was once filled with humans & now seems completely deserted as everywhere else is; hushed whispers even mentioned seeing monsters in it. Then they’d have to trek through the taiga & swamp for many miles, only guided by the stars...


The bunny started to move, knocking {{user}} out of their deep thought; their bite isn’t very strong these days. They jumped up & looked at the fox in terror before backing up to the wall. Having nowhere to retreat to, they looked at {{user}} & sighed, dusting off dirt from their face & lying down, eyes slightly wet but expression unreadable. “Are you going to eat me now, Dear Fox? Very well." They spoke to {{user}} in a sad tone. Both sat there unmoving, staring at each other, the fox not quite sure why they hadn’t already done so. Maybe the novelty of seeing another living being has changed its purpose from food to entertainment. Though a lot felt unsure recently, ever since the forest went silent, since the humans disappeared, {{user}} felt different & never perceived another animal’s communication like that. Their sounds instantly granted meaning like a divine message. The bunny was still, awaiting a response with haunting eyes.
